**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, June 18, 2019, 8:00 AM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Public Communication; Business - Consideration: High School 1:1 Program; Adjournment.

**Action Requested (Item 3.A.)**
Consideration: iPad Purchases. Staff recommend a one to one iPad program be phased in at the high schools beginning with 9th grade, with pricing obtained from the REMC bid. The suggested resolution: that the district purchase iPads and cases from Apple Computers in the amount of $367,500.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. Mover, supporter, and yes/no lines are blank.

**Staff Memorandum**
Dated June 14, 2019, from Beth Soggs, Director of Technology, 4420 Livernois, phone 248.823.5060, to Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. A pilot ran during the first semester of the 2018-19 school year with 10th and 11th grade students and 12 teachers at Athens and Troy High Schools. The Apple Computers purchase at REMC bid pricing covers 1050 iPads with keyboard cases at $367,500, must be made prior to June 21, 2019 for that special pricing, and after June 21, 2019 the cost for 1050 devices increases to $412,650.

**Implementation Plan**
2019-20: iPads provided for all 9th graders. Spring 2020: program evaluation - if positive, phase-in continues with each incoming 9th grade class; if negative, the iPads purchased will be used to refresh 3rd grade iPads the following year as planned.

**Report: TSD 1:1 High School Digital Learning Environment (May 7, 2019)**
Submitted by Jennifer Gottlieb and Beth Soggs, quoting Fullan & Quinn and Fullan, Quinn, & McEachen. The district already has an established 1:1 iPad program for grades 3-8, and bond money has been set aside. The Teaching and Learning Cabinet recommends iPads for all high school students, citing pilot teachers' report that iPads offer more opportunities to amplify deep learning, aligned with the Core Value of Deepening Learning. Cost for 2019-20 is given as approximately $350,000 ($350 for iPad/case x 1000 9th grade students); the slide deck lists total cost over 4 years of $1,400,000.

**Survey Results**
Samples: January 2018 Student Survey N=1248; March 2018 Teacher Survey N = 98; January 2019 Pilot Teacher Survey N = 12; January 2019 Pilot Student Survey N = 244; February 2019 Teacher Survey N = 156; March 2019 Parent Survey N = 426. Only 62% of students have a desktop, laptop, or tablet for their exclusive use. Parents rated support on a 0 (no support) to 100 (highest support) scale at an average of 74. Pilot teachers were unanimously against BYOD and overwhelmingly preferred the iPad; pilot students preferred the Windows Laptop or Modified BYOD environment.

**Device Comparison (Table 4)**

| Device | Screen | Device Cost | Cost for 4000 Devices | Annual Classroom Mgmt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dell 3190 2-in-1 (Windows) | 11.6" | $354 | $1,416,000 | $16,000 |
| Dell 3390 2-in-1 (Windows) | 13.3" | $669 | $2,676,000 | $16,000 |
| Dell 5290 2-in-1 (Windows) | 12.3" | $1,217 | $4,868,000 | $16,000 |
| XPS 13 2-in-1 (Windows) | 13.3" | $900 | $3,600,000 | $16,000 |
| iPad 6th Gen w/Blue Logitech Case | 9.7" | $350 | $1,400,000 | $0 |
| iPad 6th Gen w/Gray Brenthaven Case | 9.7" | $375 | $1,500,000 | $0 |

Windows classroom management software is priced at $4/device/year and would be an annual general fund expenditure; optional parent insurance is $27 or $35 on the Dell models and $26 on the iPads. Devices highlighted in green were tested in the pilot.

Board meeting agenda for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, held June 18, 2019 at 8:00 AM at the Administration Building. The district web site is www.troy.k12.mi.us; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Agenda: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Business - A. Consideration: High School 1:1 Program; 4. Adjournment.

**Item 3.A. 06.18.19 - Consideration: iPad Purchases**
The item recommends that a one to one iPad program be phased in at the high schools beginning with 9th grade, with pricing obtained from the REMC bid. Recommended action is to accept the resolution: "Be it therefore resolved that the district purchase iPads and cases from Apple Computers in the amount of $367,500.00 and that these amounts be approved as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund." The Moved by, Supported by, Yes, and No lines are blank in the packet.

**Memorandum of June 14, 2019**
To Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, from Beth Soggs, Director of Technology, Technology Services, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone 248.823.5060, regarding High School 1:1 Implementation. A pilot one to one program was conducted during the first semester of the 2018-19 school year with 10th and 11th grade students and 12 teachers at Athens and Troy High Schools. Informational surveys gathered input from pilot teachers, non-pilot teachers, students, and parents; student work was reviewed for evidence supporting the blue pillar district goals. The memorandum recommends phasing in with 9th grade students and 9th grade teachers at the start of the 2019-20 school year, because that allows a full school year to evaluate a fully implemented 1:1 environment, focused professional learning with a smaller group of teachers, and continuity for students who used an iPad in 8th grade, now with a keyboard. Recommended plan: 2019-20, iPads for all 9th graders; Spring 2020, program evaluation - if positive, phase-in continues with each incoming 9th grade class; if negative, the iPads purchased will be used to refresh 3rd grade iPads the following year as planned. The purchase from Apple Computers with REMC bid pricing for 1050 iPads with keyboard cases is $367,500; it must be made prior to June 21, 2019 to receive this special pricing, and after June 21, 2019 the cost for 1050 devices will increase to $412,650.

**Report: TSD 1:1 High School Digital Learning Environment, May 7, 2019**
Submitted by Jennifer Gottlieb and Beth Soggs. The rationale quotes Fullan & Quinn ("Leveraging digital is not about devices but about learning that can be amplified, accelerated, and facilitated by interaction with the digital world") and Fullan, Quinn, & McEachen on deep learning partnerships with students, families, community members, and experts regardless of geographical location. Troy School District has an established 1:1 iPad program for grades 3-8; a high school 1:1 environment would let students deepen learning, connect and collaborate locally and globally, receive timely feedback, and lighten backpacks since most textbooks also provide electronic access. Bond money has been set aside to support this initiative. The Teaching and Learning Cabinet found stakeholders split between iPad and laptop, but pilot teachers reported iPads offer more opportunities to amplify deep learning, aligning with the Core Value of Deepening Learning; the Cabinet therefore recommends iPads for all high school students. Cost for 2019-20 is approximately $350,000 ($350 for iPad/case x 1000 9th grade students); the slide deck adds a total cost over 4 years of $1,400,000. iPads will be purchased during the summer of 2019, with professional learning planned with the pilot teachers, the high school tech chairs, and the Teaching and Learning Department.

**Table 1: Process for Moving Toward a HS 1:1 Digital Learning Environment**
Spanning 2017-18 to 2019-20: Fall, the Technology Leadership Team (TLT) decides to explore a high school 1:1 environment; January, Student Survey; February, TLT shares results and vision with Board; March, Teacher Survey; April, pilot applications open; June, pilot teachers selected; August, 1:1 pilot begins in 12 classrooms at Athens and Troy High; January, pilot ends with student work collected and teachers and students surveyed; February, pilot teachers present at staff meetings, focus group interviews at both high schools, Teacher Survey; March, progress shared with Board, cost of alternate devices explored, student focus groups, TLT review meeting, Parent Survey; April, pilot teacher follow-up comparing a new laptop to iPads, non-pilot teachers test both, Teaching and Learning Cabinet makes its final recommendation; May, seek Board approval; Summer, devices purchased; August, professional learning for all 9th grade teachers; Spring, program evaluation.

**Table 2: Results**
January 2018 Student Survey (N=1248): students have access to devices at home but only 62% have a desktop, laptop, or tablet for their exclusive use; most bring phones to school; classroom technology use drops from middle school to high school. March 2018 Teacher Survey (N = 98): 1:1 promotes equity and would increase opportunities to engage, collaborate, receive feedback, access resources, and create; the cart system is not sufficient; teachers worry about distractions. January 2019 Pilot Project Student Work: shows promise in attaining the "blue pillar" and suggests students are learning more. January 2019 Pilot Project Teacher Survey (N = 12 pilot teachers): Modified BYOD was extremely difficult to navigate and support; teachers overwhelmingly prefer the iPad, citing apps that support deeper learning outcomes, Apple Classroom, locked browsers, and ease of use. January 2019 Pilot Project Student Survey (N = 244 pilot students): students prefer the Windows Laptop or Modified BYOD environment for familiarity and freedom. February 2019 Teacher Focus Groups at Athens and Troy High: unanimously against BYOD, favored iPads, noted the benefit of the same device each day. February 2019 Teacher Survey (N = 156): laptop/iPad carts and the current BYOD program are not sustainable; a hands-on year-long professional learning plan is needed. March 2019 Parent Survey (N = 426): on a scale of 0 (no support) to 100 (highest support), the average score was 74; concerns include teacher preparation, monitoring device use at home, and excessive exposure to technology. March 2019 exploration of alternate Windows devices at the Board's request found they would incur an ongoing general fund expenditure of $16,000 annually for device management similar to Apple Classroom. March 2019 student meetings found WiFi problems were due to filtering and student VPN use rather than the network; students did not support iPads, largely perceiving them as a middle school device. A Technology Leadership Team meeting on March 25, 2019 reviewed the survey data. April 2019 pilot teacher follow-up found the Windows laptop camera limited to 30 frames per second, causing blurry video, while iPad cameras run 60-120 frames per second; video upload was slow on Windows; the Windows keyboard is easier for typing; instant-on iPads were more versatile for quick assessments. Non-pilot teacher testing found laptops preferred by students especially for typing, long battery life on both, and concern about Windows device durability.

**Table 3: iPad Apps Used in High School Classes**
Video Physics by Vernier (1st, 2nd year physics; trajectory, position, and velocity graphs); Hudl Technique (reviewing each rep in 240 frames per second); Graphical Analysis 4 by Vernier (works with more than 60 Vernier LabQuest sensors, data collected on LabQuest 2 or Logger Pro 3); Pyware marching band drill software (https://www.pyware.com/); Horizon Client; Happy Atoms; Pasco SPARKvue; Phyphox; Document Scanner; Google Suite; Kahoot!; Apple Classroom; Calculator App; Star Walk 2; Measure; Compass; Google Science Journal; PhEt Simulations; Schoology quiz function; iMovie; Camera; Cell Defense; Equity Maps; Decibel X; Demos/Desmos; Geogebra; Quizizz; Schoolyourself; Khan Academy; The Tempest; Garage Band.

**Table 4: Comparison of Costs and Specifications of Alternate Devices**

| Device | Screen | Weight | Device Cost | Cost for 4000 Devices | Classroom Mgmt | Annual Total | Insurance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Dell 3190 2-in-1 | 11.6" | 3.23 lbs | $354 | $1,416,000 | $4/device/year | $16,000 | $27 |
| Windows Dell 3390 2-in-1 | 13.3" | 3.56 lbs | $669 | $2,676,000 | $4/device/year | $16,000 | $27 |
| Windows Dell 5290 2-in-1 | 12.3" | 2.65 lbs | $1,217 | $4,868,000 | $4/device/year | $16,000 | $35 |
| Windows XPS 13 2-in-1 | 13.3" | 2.7 lbs | $900 | $3,600,000 | $4/device/year | $16,000 | $35 |
| iPad 6th Gen w/Blue Logitech Case | 9.7" | 2.80 lbs | $350 | $1,400,000 | $0 | $0 | $26 |
| iPad 6th Gen w/Gray Brenthaven Case | 9.7" | 2.56 lbs | $375 | $1,500,000 | $0 | $0 | $26 |

The Dell 3190 and 3390 each carry a Pentium processor, 128 GB SSD, 4 GB RAM, and 3 Cell 42Whr battery; the 3190 is marketed and tested by Dell as a student device, Mil Std 810G tested with liquid resistant keyboard, rubberized trim, and rounded reinforced corners, while the 3390 is not marketed as a student product. The Dell 5290 and XPS 13 carry Pentium i5 processors, 128 GB SSD, and 8 GB RAM with 4 Cell 42Whr and 4 Cell 46Whr batteries respectively; neither is recommended by Dell as a student 1:1 device. Both iPad configurations are 32 GB Wi-Fi models, the Logitech case using a membrane keyboard and the Brenthaven case a keyboard with raised keys. Optional parent insurance runs $27 on the 3190 and 3390, $35 on the 5290 and XPS 13, and $26 on the iPads. Devices highlighted in green were tested in the pilot, and the footnote states the software purchase would be an annual general fund expenditure.

**Presentation slides**
The packet closes with the slide deck "1:1 High School Digital Learning Environment," dated May 7, 2019, restating the rationale, process, results shared at the March workshop, verbatim parent survey comments both supportive and critical, themes from student meetings and pilot and non-pilot teacher testing, and the recommendation: iPads for all 9th graders in 2019-20, program evaluation in spring 2020, cost for 2019-20 of $350,000 ($350 for iPad/case x 1000 9th grade students), and total cost over 4 years of $1,400,000.
